question: Which renewal looks most at risk, and why?

resolution.read_instruction: Extract every statement in this call that bears on the customer's likelihood to renew or stay: expressed dissatisfaction, complaints, unresolved issues, usage or adoption levels, budget or pricing pressure, competitor mentions, stakeholder changes, explicit threats to cancel or not renew, and any positive signals of commitment or expansion. Include the speaker and a short quote for each, and note whether OrbitFlow staff addressed the issue.
assumptions: 'Renewal' is interpreted as the Renewal call type (CALL-011, CALL-012, CALL-013), so the comparison across renewal calls can be made from the extracted risk signals.
'Most at risk' is a judgement that must be made by comparing the extracted signals across the renewal calls, since a single call cannot show relative risk.

findings.speaker: Devan Shah
findings.quote: Resolution times on anything involving the SAP connector have been terrible. We had a ticket open for nineteen days in July.
findings.context: Customer reports SAP connector resolution times have been terrible; a ticket sat for eleven days after a nineteen-day open period in July. — Unresolved support issue (resolution time, not response time); vendor acknowledged and offered a named escalation contact but no resolution SLA.

findings.speaker: Ruth Adeyemi
findings.quote: It sat for eleven days and there's no good explanation.
findings.context: Vendor admitted the SAP ticket fell between teams and offered a named engineer escalation contact, but declined to promise a resolution SLA. — OrbitFlow staff addressed the issue; no resolution commitment given.

findings.speaker: Devan Shah
findings.quote: The named contact is more useful than a promise, honestly.
findings.context: Customer's platform manager says the named contact is more useful than a promise, but the issue remains a grievance. — Mild acceptance of vendor response; underlying dissatisfaction persists.

findings.speaker: Ruth Adeyemi
findings.quote: You've exceeded your contracted run volume in four of the last six months. June was twenty-two percent over.
findings.context: Customer is running over contracted run volume and the run tier is inadequate; June was 22% over and four of six months exceeded. — Usage pressure; vendor agreed the tier is wrong and proposed moving to 400k runs.

findings.speaker: Devan Shah
findings.quote: From our side we did nothing wrong and it cost us twenty thousand runs.
findings.context: March retry-storm overage (about 20,000 runs) was a point of frustration; customer felt it was not their fault and questioned what OrbitFlow changed. — Vendor partly attributed to configuration; vendor admitted it should have addressed this in April; retry-config session booked.

findings.speaker: Ruth Adeyemi
findings.quote: You've got nine builders licensed and four of them haven't published anything in six months.
findings.context: Nine licensed builders with four dormant; customer's seat count is being reduced to seven, which is a renewal scrutiny risk and a reduction in spend. — Adoption weakness; vendor addressed it by proposing seven active seats; customer questioned the reduction.

findings.speaker: Fiona Bright
findings.quote: The depot exception routing. Without question. Everything else we could go back to doing the old way and survive.
findings.context: Customer expressed strong positive value on the depot exceptions workflow, which is the core reason to stay. — Strong commitment signal; the depot exceptions routing would be painful to lose.

findings.speaker: Fiona Bright
findings.quote: Braced for "here's a fifteen percent uplift, sign here."
findings.context: Customer finance review and price sensitivity: customer expected a 15% uplift and was relieved by 7%; needs finance director sign-off with clear line items, decision expected week of the fifteenth. — Budget pressure; vendor committed to itemised proposal by Friday; renewal expires 18 October.

findings.speaker: Devan Shah
findings.quote: Because when something breaks I can answer the question in four minutes instead of half a day.
findings.context: Customer positive about run history and quality of life from the platform; supports continued use. — Value signal from platform manager.

findings.speaker: Fiona Bright
findings.quote: Yes. Let's do that.
findings.context: Customer intends to expand into supplier onboarding and agreed to a visibility phase; expansion signals commitment. — Positive expansion signal; contingent on instrumentation decision before Christmas.

findings.speaker: Ruth Adeyemi
findings.quote: Usage has dropped about forty percent since March.
findings.context: Usage has dropped about forty percent since March, per OrbitFlow's Ruth Adeyemi, and she raised the renewal and dissatisfaction concern directly. — Vendor framing of renewal risk; opens the call. Vendor-stated usage figure.

findings.speaker: Graham Attwood
findings.quote: I inherited this. Ravi bought it, Ravi implemented it, Ravi left in February, and I picked it up in March with about forty minutes of handover.
findings.context: Customer says the account was inherited with minimal handover after the original champion left, and the customer's own team owns the gap. — Stakeholder change driving adoption problems; vendor acknowledged failure to re-onboard.

findings.speaker: Ruth Adeyemi
findings.quote: Six of them haven't run successfully in the last ninety days.
findings.context: Six of fourteen production workflows have not run successfully in 90 days, and one 'TEMP' workflow has been failing since January with alerts going to a dead shared mailbox nobody read. — Unresolved technical issues; vendor says it does not proactively monitor at this tier.

findings.speaker: Graham Attwood
findings.quote: I don't know. That's the honest answer. The claims director changed in April and the new one has a different view about where triage should happen.
findings.context: Customer is unsure the original reason for buying (claims triage) still holds; the new claims director wants triage in Guidewire, a potential loss of half the use case. — Competitor/alternative platform pressure and stakeholder change.

findings.speaker: Graham Attwood
findings.quote: Nobody's building anything. We've got four builder licences. One person uses it.
findings.context: Only one builder has ever built workflows; four builder licences are paid for but unused, and the sole builder has been on leave since June. Two-person training attempt in July did not take. — Low adoption and bus-factor risk; vendor agreed enablement is its responsibility.

findings.speaker: Nadia Rahman
findings.quote: Our security standard requires SSO for anything holding claims data.
findings.context: Customer is paying for Enterprise tier but using very little of it; the vendor says Enterprise is likely not worth it and Growth tier would lose SSO, which security requires. — Budget/pricing pressure; Growth downgrade not viable due to SSO requirement.

findings.speaker: Nadia Rahman
findings.quote: it's the kind of thing that means I don't raise tickets any more, and then you look at the data and conclude we're happy.
findings.context: Customer says support tickets were answered within SLA but responses were unhelpful, so they raise fewer tickets; low ticket volume may hide dissatisfaction. — Unresolved support complaint; vendor acknowledged it.

findings.speaker: Leo Grant
findings.quote: Your current contract auto-renews with sixty days' notice, which means your notice deadline is the thirtieth of September.
findings.context: Current contract auto-renews with 60 days' notice, so the notice deadline is 30 September; customer was unaware and must serve notice to keep options open. — Renewal mechanics creating a time-bound risk; vendor disclosed it.

findings.speaker: Nadia Rahman
findings.quote: I don't think the product is the problem. I think we implemented it badly, one person owned it
findings.context: Customer's stated concern is that the problem is implementation and ownership, not the product; this is a positive signal of possible commitment. — Customer-side view that contrasts with the risk picture.

findings.speaker: Graham Attwood
findings.quote: I'm not going to pretend I'm enthusiastic.
findings.context: Graham's stated renewal sentiment is not enthusiastic; he says he is not pretending to be enthusiastic and that the outcome is open. — Overall commitment signal, mixed: no explicit cancel threat but low enthusiasm.

findings.speaker: Ruth Adeyemi
findings.quote: You're renewing in November, usage is healthy, six builders all active, error rate under one percent, and the only change is a seven percent standard uplift.
findings.context: Renewal is in November and usage is healthy: six builders all active with error rate under one percent; the only change is a seven percent standard uplift. — Vendor (Ruth) framing of the renewal; positive adoption signal, stated by OrbitFlow staff rather than the customer.

findings.speaker: Tobias Lund
findings.quote: Fifteen minutes times about four hundred incidents a month.
findings.context: Customer names a concrete AI use case with significant volume (about 400 incidents a month, roughly fifteen minutes saved each), which supports adoption and expansion. — Customer-quantified value; vendor (Nina) advised testing on fifty historical incidents before relying on the estimate.

findings.speaker: Tobias Lund
findings.quote: We used to take eleven days to bring a new managed detection client live and now it's four.
findings.context: Customer says the onboarding workflow has been the best outcome, cutting managed detection client go-live from eleven days to four and making it consistent. — Positive value realization; customer-reported success.

findings.speaker: Grace Okonkwo
findings.quote: It's not a criticism of the product. It's a criticism of us, and slightly of you for not mentioning it eighteen months ago.
findings.context: Customer is frustrated that they had no change control on production and did not know version history existed after eighteen months; this is framed as a criticism of their own team and slightly of OrbitFlow for not raising it. — Dissatisfaction, but directed mostly at Halberd's own process; the vendor acknowledged it.

findings.speaker: Tobias Lund
findings.quote: We've had two people ask about a mobile experience.
findings.context: Customer raised a mobile experience gap for analysts approving from phones; the vendor said the product is not a mobile product and proposed a Teams/Slack approval workaround, which was scoped as exploratory. — Unresolved feature gap; OrbitFlow staff addressed it honestly but did not commit to a solution.

findings.speaker: Grace Okonkwo
findings.quote: Right. I'm supportive, subject to the four written answers.
findings.context: Customer's CISO has conditions on AI use and wants written answers before going live; the AI enablement is contingent on those answers and a fifty-incident test, so expansion is conditional rather than certain. — Conditional commitment; outstanding vendor follow-ups on permissions, retention, model list, and subprocessor documentation.

findings.speaker: Ruth Adeyemi
findings.quote: Renewal is agreed subject to papers — seven percent, no other changes, AI consumption estimate included.
findings.context: Renewal is agreed subject to papers, with OrbitFlow to send renewal papers by Wednesday and the customer to review clause fourteen on training. — Commitment signal; the renewal is described as agreed by vendor summary, and customer confirmed the summary as accurate.

findings.speaker: Grace Okonkwo
findings.quote: Seven percent on a number that size is not worth an hour of my life.
findings.context: Overall renewal risk appears low: the customer is calm about price, adoption is healthy, expansion is being discussed, and no cancellation threat or competitor mention appears in this call. — Inferred from the whole call; no explicit churn threat or competitor reference was found.

rejected_findings.claim: Vendor offered a six-month renewal with re-implementation and enablement included, or non-renewal. Customer had said two weeks earlier they would have not renewed.
rejected_findings.quote: If I'm not enthusiastic. If you'd asked me two weeks ago I'd have said we're not renewing.
rejected_findings.speaker: Graham Attwood (customer)
rejected_findings.reason: quote not found in cited turns

rejected_findings.claim: Customer accepts the seven percent uplift without concern, calling it not worth an hour of effort.
rejected_findings.quote: That's fine. ... Seven percent on a number that size is not worth an hour of my life.
rejected_findings.speaker: Grace Okonkwo
rejected_findings.reason: quote not found in cited turns

rejected_findings.claim: Customer describes renewal as the fastest conversation and expresses intent to turn on AI features in a controlled way, which signals expansion interest.
rejected_findings.quote: Now I want to turn it on, in one place, under conditions I define. ... That's acceptable. Possibly better, actually.
rejected_findings.speaker: Grace Okonkwo
rejected_findings.reason: quote not found in cited turns

draft.answer: Pinewood Insurance (CALL-012) looks most at risk of the three renewals. Usage is down, adoption is thin, the original use case is in doubt, and the customer is lukewarm, with an approaching notice deadline [C1][C2][C3][C4]. Lumen Retail Group has real grievances but strong commitment signals [C5], and Halberd Security appears low risk [C6].

claims.text: Pinewood Insurance: OrbitFlow's Ruth Adeyemi said usage has dropped about 40% since March, and six of fourteen production workflows have not run successfully in 90 days. One 'TEMP' workflow has been failing since January, with alerts going to a dead shared mailbox nobody read. The vendor said it does not proactively monitor at this tier.

Pinewood's adoption and ownership have collapsed. Graham Attwood inherited the account in March with about forty minutes of handover after champion Ravi left in February. Only one builder has ever built workflows, four builder licences are unused, and the sole builder has been on leave since June. A July two-person training attempt did not take.

Pinewood's original use case is in doubt. Attwood is unsure claims triage still holds, since the new claims director (changed in April) wants triage in Guidewire, a potential loss of half the use case. Attwood said he is not going to pretend to be enthusiastic. This sentiment finding is inferred, with the outcome described as open.

Pinewood faces pricing and timing pressure. The customer pays for Enterprise but uses little of it, and the vendor said Enterprise is likely not worth it. A downgrade to Growth would lose SSO, which security requires (Nadia Rahman). The contract auto-renews with 60 days' notice, so the deadline is 30 September, which the customer was unaware of (Leo Grant). Rahman also said tickets met SLA but were unhelpful, so she raises fewer tickets and low volume may hide dissatisfaction.

Lumen Retail Group has real grievances. SAP connector resolution has been terrible, with a ticket open 19 days in July and sitting 11 days; Ruth Adeyemi gave a named engineer contact but no resolution SLA (Devan Shah said the contact is more useful than a promise). The customer exceeded contracted runs in four of six months (June 22% over) and was frustrated by a March retry-storm overage of about 20,000 runs. Four of nine builders are dormant and seats are being cut to seven. Even so, Fiona Bright said depot exception routing is the core reason to stay, Shah values the run history, and the customer agreed to a supplier-onboarding visibility phase. It was relieved by a 7% uplift (it expected 15%) but needs finance director sign-off, with a decision expected the week of the fifteenth and expiry on 18 October.

Halberd Security appears low risk. Ruth Adeyemi described usage as healthy (six active builders, error rate under 1%) with only a 7% uplift. Renewal was agreed subject to papers, with clause fourteen on training to be reviewed. Tobias Lund cited onboarding go-live cut from 11 days to 4. Residual items are conditional AI expansion pending CISO Grace Okonkwo's four written answers, an unresolved mobile gap, and a change-control complaint aimed mostly at the customer's own team. The low-risk overall view is inferred.

Pinewood's stakeholders offer a counterpoint: Nadia Rahman said the product is not the problem and that the issue is bad implementation and single-person ownership, which may mean the account is recoverable.

conflicts.topic: Pinewood: product vs. implementation as the cause
conflicts.description: Rahman says the product is not the problem and the issue is implementation and ownership, while Attwood questions whether the original claims-triage use case still holds and is not enthusiastic.
